A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TDSM research, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v3 ends with references; v4 adds Supplementary Material comprising Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v3 reports original recognition experiments on NTU-60, NTU-120 and PKU-MMD, together with loss, feature, timestep and noise ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Kinetics evaluations, backbone and prediction-target experiments, and class-level analyses.

M1.justification: The main TDSM procedure, triplet diffusion loss and one-step classifier are retained. Appendix A.1 adds an experimentally implemented variant predicting clean skeleton features instead of noise, which v3 mentioned only as future work. The expanded CrossDiT specification documents the existing architecture without establishing a redesign.

E1.justification: Tables 7–8 add actual zero-shot evaluations on Kinetics-200 and Kinetics-400, substantially expanding dataset and action-class coverage beyond the retained NTU and PKU-MMD experiments. Kinetics was cited but not evaluated in v3.

E2.justification: v4 introduces DeViSE in the Kinetics comparisons and adds RGB-assisted BSZSL on the retained NTU splits in Table 9. The comparator memberships in the original Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify Kinetics class splits, one-versus-seven-prompt PURLS controls and a U-Net-versus-DiT comparison. Appendix B.4 also describes inference at T/2, including 50 when T=100, while the retained main text states 25 for all experiments. The actual protocol for nondefault T remains unresolved; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v4 adds clean-feature prediction sensitivity experiments in Figure 5, a backbone ablation in Table 12, and split-specific and class-confusion analyses in Table 10 and Figures 6–7. These substantially extend investigation of noise stability, architectural choice and recognition failures beyond the retained original ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly discloses random seed 2025. Averaging ten Gaussian noise realizations and displaying their variation were already present in v3; Figure 5 extends that practice without establishing an increase in independent training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figure 4 retain their results, but substantial new results appear. Table 7 reports 38.18% for TDSM versus 32.22% for seven-prompt PURLS on Kinetics-200 180/20. Table 9 shows TDSM winning three splits but trailing BSZSL 74.15% to 77.69% on NTU-120 110/10. Split-level, backbone and prediction-target findings are also added.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds explicit mathematical definitions of feature embeddings, conditional modulation and joint attention in Equations 16–19. The original diffusion formulation, triplet loss and zero-shot assumptions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Despite retitling, the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core claims: a first diffusion-based ZSAR framework, discriminative alignment through the triplet diffusion loss, and substantial benchmark outperformance. Additional supplementary evidence does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: The existing noise limitation moves to Appendix A and gains discussion of the stability–accuracy tradeoff from clean-feature prediction. Appendix B.3 newly explains success through distinct motion patterns and failures through similar hand movements and unavailable object context. Appendix B.4 adds a training–inference mismatch argument, substantially expanding interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E and Table 13 disclose CrossDiT operations, 12 blocks and 12 attention heads, hidden dimensions, token counts, feature shapes, prompt generation and tuning provenance. These fill substantial documentation gaps without proving changes to existing settings. Appendix E's two-description account remains unreconciled with Appendix B.5's single-sentence account.

R1.justification: Appendices C, D and F substantially expand positioning against diffusion-based motion, pose and action-detection research and supervised skeleton-recognition methods. They also clarify framework-level novelty relative to existing DiT/MMDiT components. Earlier cited works are retained alongside numerous newly discussed works.

P1.justification: The retained main narrative is largely verbatim. Changes include the title, acknowledgements, supplementary signposting and relocation of the limitations subsection to Appendix A. New discussions are organized into Appendices A–F, without extensive rewriting of the existing main text.

P2.justification: Figures 5–8 add prediction-target curves, confusion matrices with per-class accuracy plots, and a detailed CrossDiT diagram. Tables 7–13 add benchmark, split, backbone, conceptual-comparison and feature-shape displays. Existing tables also move within the reflowed main text, producing a substantial expansion of visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially reduces v3's CrossDiT documentation gap through architectural equations, a detailed diagram and implementation settings. Kinetics evaluations and targeted robustness and failure analyses make the retained method's strengths and limitations considerably more assessable. Conflicting prompt-count and timestep descriptions still limit exact reproduction, but the gains in technical transparency and empirical support outweigh these weaknesses.
